key_insight: STIRC2025 introduces a benchmark for evaluating point-tracking algorithms in surgical video using infrared surgical tattoo data. It helps standardize how well methods can follow tissue landmarks over time, which is essential for downstream surgical AI tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a dedicated, quantifiable benchmark for point tracking in surgery. Without such an evaluation framework, it is difficult to compare methods for tracking anatomical or artificial landmarks reliably in surgical settings.
method: Defines the Surgical Tattoos in Infrared (STIR) dataset as the evaluation benchmark for point tracking.
Runs a challenge framework where participants submit tracking algorithms for standardized scoring.
Quantifies performance of methods on surgical point tracking to enable fair comparison across approaches.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a reproducible benchmark for developing and testing surgical tracking models. It supports progress toward more reliable systems for segmentation, 3D reconstruction, autonomous scanning, and other surgical robotics tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input surgical infrared video -> point tracker -> tracked landmark outputs

paper_title: Point Tracking in Surgery--The 2025 Surgical Tattoos in Infrared Challenge (STIRC2025)
paper_authors: Adam Schmidt, Mert Asim Karaoglu, Zijian Wu, Jiaming Zhang, Yuxin Chen
